draft.title: Regulating water balance
card: The body must keep the water in its blood and tissues within a narrow range. Water is lost in urine, sweat and breath, and gained from food and drink.
When the body is short of water, the blood becomes more concentrated. Receptors in the hypothalamus detect this change.

The hypothalamus signals the pituitary gland to release more antidiuretic hormone (ADH) into the blood. ADH makes the kidneys reabsorb more water back into the blood, so less water leaves in urine and the urine is small in volume and concentrated.
When the body has too much water, less ADH is released. The kidneys reabsorb less water, so more water leaves in a larger volume of dilute urine.
draft.remember: Short of water: more ADH, more water reabsorbed, less urine. Too much water: less ADH, more urine.

a.q: What does ADH do when the body is short of water?
opts: It makes the kidneys reabsorb more water into the blood
It makes the kidneys release more water into the urine
It makes the sweat glands release more water onto the skin
It makes the hypothalamus stop detecting blood concentration
a.why: ADH acts on the kidneys so that more water returns to the blood. This saves water for the body. Sending more water into urine would make the shortage worse.
a.clue: Think about whether the body needs to save water or get rid of it.

b.q: Jin plays football on a hot day, sweats a lot and drinks nothing for two hours. What happens to his ADH release and urine?
opts: More ADH is released, and his urine is more concentrated
More ADH is released, and his urine is more dilute
Less ADH is released, and his urine is more concentrated
Less ADH is released, and his urine is more dilute
b.why: Sweating without drinking makes his blood more concentrated, so more ADH is released. The kidneys reabsorb more water, leaving a small volume of concentrated urine. Dilute urine would waste water he cannot spare.
b.clue: Losing water makes the blood more concentrated, so the body must save water.

a.best: It makes the kidneys reabsorb more water into the blood

b.best: More ADH is released, and his urine is more concentrated
